title: CCNA vs CCST Networking
intro: Cisco's two entry points, $175 apart: the $125 true-beginner checkpoint or the $300 credential employers actually recognize. The right answer depends entirely on where you're standing.

a.name: Cisco CCNA
a.tagline: The industry-standard networking credential — 200-301, $300, 120 minutes, the cert that gets interviews.

b.name: CCST Networking
b.tagline: Cisco's $125 ground floor — 100-150, 50 minutes, free official training, designed as the first step toward CCNA.

verdict: If you're an adult committed to a networking career: CCNA, full stop — CCST gives no exam credit toward it, and hiring filters search for CCNA, not CCST. Pick CCST Networking when you're a student, when $300 plus study materials is genuinely out of reach, or when you're honestly unsure networking is your lane and want a $125 structured answer before committing. CCST's real product is the free 70-hour NetAcad path with a cheap proof-of-completion attached — used that way, it's excellent.

rows.label: Exam
rows.a: 200-301, $300, 120 minutes — question count not published (simulations included)

rows.label: Recognition
rows.a: The most-cited networking cert at its level — the interview-getter
rows.b: Almost no job filters search it yet; growing via the high-school pipeline

rows.label: Audience
rows.a: Committed networking careers; assumes real study commitment
rows.b: Students, budget starts, and the genuinely undecided

rows.label: Training
rows.a: Books, videos, Packet Tracer — typically $50–200 in materials
rows.b: Free official NetAcad path (~70 hours) covers it entirely

rows.label: Validity
rows.a: 3 years, renewable via exams or CE credits
rows.b: 5 years if earned on or after July 15, 2025 (lifetime before); exam-only renewal

rows.label: Bridge between them
rows.b: Curricular only: the NetAcad path flows into the CCNA series, but no exam credit or discount transfers

pick_a_if: You're committed to networking and job-hunting within a year
You can invest 3–6 months of real study including lab time
You want the credential that actually appears in job filters
pick_b_if: You're a student — especially if your school offers it through Certiport
Budget is the genuine constraint and $125 is the ceiling
You're testing whether networking pulls you before committing months
You want a milestone partway through the free NetAcad curriculum
both_note: The sequence works exactly as Cisco designed it — CCST as the confidence checkpoint, CCNA as the destination — as long as you know nothing transfers on paper. Momentum is the real bridge: take CCNA while the CCST fundamentals are fresh, not a year later.

faq.question: Does CCST Networking give any credit toward CCNA?
faq.answer: No — no exam credit, no discount. The bridge is purely curricular: the free NetAcad path that preps CCST flows directly into the CCNA course series. Your knowledge carries; your $125 doesn't.

faq.question: Will employers care about CCST at all?
faq.answer: Mostly not yet, honestly. It appears in almost no job filters — CCNA, Network+, and A+ own that space. Its value is proof-of-readiness, momentum, and the genuinely good free training behind it. As a resume line next to a homelab story it does no harm; as a substitute for CCNA it doesn't work.

faq.question: I'm 30+ and switching careers — is CCST beneath me?
faq.answer: Not beneath you, just possibly redundant. If you're committed, the $125 buys more as CCNA study materials. But if 'committed' is doing heavy lifting in that sentence — if you're actually still deciding — a $125 structured test-drive with free training is the cheapest honest answer in IT. Deciding is a legitimate use of money.
